title: introduce-route-auth-hint-header-and-compat-adapter-for-proxied-streaming-tool-calls
author: Priya Natarajan
description: Motivation: streaming tool calls and chained function/tool workflows suffer from fragile header semantics when requests are forwarded through edge proxies and gateway adapters (CORS preflight and streaming handshake especially). This PR adds a lightweight, opt-in per-route hint header (X-RW-Route-Auth) and a small compatibility adapter for OpenAI-compat endpoints so downstream proxies can safely forward scoped auth tokens and a short-lived signing bridge header. Design: 1) X-RW-Route-Auth (value: hint tokens or route id) allows the API gateway to advertise per-route auth expectations to downstream workers without exposing project keys. 2) RW-Signed-Bridge is an asymmetric-signed envelope (opaque string) the gateway can attach when a request needs to be proxied to an external tool runtime; workers validate the signature against a rotation-aware public key store. 3) Backwards compatible fallback: if neither header is present we keep existing project/org key semantics. 4) CORS: preflight responses are extended to include the new headers in Access-Control-Expose-Headers and Access-Control-Allow-Headers where appropriate. Implementation notes: server/proxy handles hint parsing and short-circuits token forwarding only for routes flagged in route config; a new compat layer in api/openai adapts X-RW-Route-Auth to the legacy X-Project header for older SDKs. Testing and rollout: feature-gated behind "route-auth-hint" feature flag (on by default for dedicated infra), unit+integration tests added, and manual canary in perf-canary for 48h before global merge. See linked Linear tickets for edge-case acceptance criteria.
commits: feat(proxy): add hint header parsing and validation for X-RW-Route-Auth
feat(openai-compat): map route hints to legacy X-Project header when compat mode enabled
feat(security): implement RW-Signed-Bridge validation and public key rotation consumer
docs: describe new headers and CORS implications in docs/auth.md
test: add integration test for streaming tool call passthrough with signed bridge
review_comments: Evan Morales: We should confirm the performance impact on hot path—parsing & verifying RW-Signed-Bridge must not allocate heavily during streaming. Can we move validation to a lightweight fast-path?

Priya Natarajan: Good point—validator uses a fast header parse and async signature verification pipeline for the initial handshake; streaming frames proceed before full verification if hint header is present, with a short TTL to allow fallback. Added bench numbers in PR description.
Sophie Laurent: CORS change looks fine but ensure Access-Control-Expose-Headers only lists trusted headers for browser clients. Please update docs with explicit examples for preflight flows.
Priya Natarajan: Updated docs/auth.md with explicit example curl + browser preflight snippets and note about restricting expose-list for public routes.
Daniel Kim: What about replay risk of RW-Signed-Bridge? Need explicit TTL + nonce in the envelope.
Priya Natarajan: RW-Signed-Bridge includes issuance timestamp and short nonce. Validator rejects if timestamp > 60s old. Added unit test for replay protection.
release_notes: Introduce X-RW-Route-Auth and RW-Signed-Bridge to improve auth forwarding for proxied streaming/tool calls. Backward-compatible; opt-in via route config. Note CORS preflight updates required for browser clients.
